about:
Eight room-temperature values of the ultrasonic nonlinearity parameter of solids, beta_avg, from Table 6.5: five crystal structures or bonding classes (zincblende, fluorite, face-centred cubic metals and inert-gas solids, body-centred cubic metals) and three named materials (NaCl, fused silica and a YBCO ceramic), each with its bonding. The prose beside the table says each value is the average over the three pure-mode directions [100], [110] and [111] of a cubic crystal, which differ but not greatly; for a structure it is also an average over the solids that share it.

The parameter is the page's own beta, defined in its Eq. (6.76) as -(3 + K3/K2) with K2 and K3 the second- and third-order elastic coefficients of the propagation direction. The page's Table 6.6 gives the same parameter for a liquid as B/A + 2 and for an ideal gas as gamma + 1, so a solid's beta compares with a liquid's B/A + 2 and not with its B/A. The table credits no source.

rows.name: Flourite
rows.note: Printed "Flourite", the fluorite structure of CaF2; the name is kept as printed and the spelling is registered in docs/ERRATA.md.

rows.name: Fused silica
rows.note: The only negative value of the table, and printed with its minus sign: by the page's definition beta = -(3 + K3/K2), a negative beta means K3/K2 is above -3, the opposite of the crystals. The prose beside the table gives the range as 2 to 15 for cubic crystals, and fused silica, an isotropic glass, is not one.

rows.name: YBa2Cu3O7−δ (ceramic)
rows.note: The page sets the formula with subscripts, YBa₂Cu₃O₇₋δ, a ceramic superconductor.
